project.name: penguin
project.description: A modern desktop API client for gRPC-Web, gRPC, and SDK testing, built with Tauri 2, React 19, and Rust. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.summary: Decrypts a vault envelope by unwrapping the content key with an available recipient token and decrypting the payload.

nodes.name: reencryptVaultJson
nodes.summary: Re-encrypts an existing vault envelope to a new recipient set, preserving the underlying plaintext.

nodes.name: unwrapVaultEnvelope
nodes.summary: Validates and unwraps a vault envelope, recovering the AES content key from a matching recipient entry.

nodes.name: deriveWrapKey
nodes.summary: Derives a per-recipient AES wrapping key from the recipient token using a key-derivation routine.

nodes.name: computeVaultDiff

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what Penguin is: a modern desktop API client for gRPC-Web, gRPC, REST, Redis, and SDK testing, built with Tauri 2, React 19, and a Rust backend. It documents the feature set, tech stack, project structure, and release flow, giving you the roadmap for the rest of this tour. Keep its mental model of frontend (React) talking to a Rust backend over Tauri commands as you read the code.

tour.title: Frontend Entry Point
tour.description: main.tsx is where the React frontend boots. Before mounting the React root it hydrates persisted state from the database, installs an error-log sink, and syncs the package cache version — so the UI starts already aware of saved data. From here control flows into the root App component that wires every feature together.
tour.languageLesson: React 19 mounts via createRoot(...).render(). Side-effect setup that must finish before first paint (here, state hydration) runs imperatively before render rather than inside a component effect.

tour.title: Application Shell
tour.description: App.tsx is the root component that assembles the whole product: it wires the API client, REST, Redis, vault, database, browser, and docs modules, registers global keyboard shortcuts, and owns the protocol/tab state that switches between features. Read this as the table of contents for the UI layer — each module it imports is a subsystem the later steps explore.

tour.title: Global State Store
tour.description: store.ts is the central Zustand store that holds the app's reactive state — open tabs, environments, request history, headers — and threads in the persistence helpers. Almost every feature reads and writes through it, so understanding its shape unlocks how UI actions turn into persisted changes. This is the hub that connects the App shell from Step 3 to the persistence layer in Step 5.
tour.languageLesson: Zustand stores are plain hooks: components subscribe to slices of state and re-render only when that slice changes, avoiding the boilerplate of React Context + reducers.

tour.title: Persistence & Sync Core
tour.description: This tightly-coupled cluster is Penguin's persistence backbone. penguin-db.ts is the Tauri invoke wrapper over the SQLite store; app-persistence.ts caches those values in memory and migrates legacy localStorage keys into the database; environment-persistence.ts and environment-sync.ts layer per-protocol environment snapshots and remote-config merging on top. Together they implement the Postman-style local storage model the store from Step 4 depends on.

tour.title: REST Client Module
tour.description: The REST feature is the most fleshed-out client. rest-types.ts (the single most depended-upon file in the codebase) defines the vocabulary — requests, collections, environments, auth, cookies, history, responses — that the rest of the module shares. RestPage.tsx is the top-level page orchestrating projects, collections, tabs, and the editor, while rest-keychain.ts bridges to the Rust secret keychain and cookie store so credentials never sit in plaintext UI state.
tour.languageLesson: rest-types.ts is a barrel of shared interfaces. Centralizing domain types in one module gives every consumer a single source of truth and is why this file has the highest fan-in in the project.

tour.title: AI Knowledge Vault
tour.description: The vault stores credentials and knowledge that power AI-assisted workflows. types.ts defines its domain — projects, environments, credentials, and built-in 'kinds' — and is the second most depended-upon file in the project. VaultPage.tsx wires the sidebar, kind rail, main panel, and editors, and manages project state, persistence, Lark push/sync, and undo, mirroring the REST module's page-orchestration pattern from Step 6.

tour.title: Tauri Rust Backend Entry
tour.description: Crossing into the Rust side, lib.rs is the Tauri application entry point. It wires the plugins, registers every command handler through the invoke handler, and bootstraps the product database plus background watchers. This is the backend mirror of App.tsx — the place where all the Rust subsystems the frontend invokes are assembled.
tour.languageLesson: Rust/Tauri: the invoke_handler with generate_handler! macro registers backend functions as commands the JavaScript frontend can call by name, forming the IPC bridge between the two languages.

tour.title: SQLite Data Layer & Engines
tour.description: These modules are the engines behind the frontend clients. db.rs is the core SQLite data layer providing the product database connection and CRUD for settings, saved requests, history, and error logs — the Rust counterpart to penguin-db.ts from Step 5. rest/mod.rs declares the REST submodules and shared request/response/secret types, and redis/commands.rs exposes the Redis command surface (connect, scan, and per-type read/write).

tour.title: Bundled MCP Server
tour.description: Penguin ships a Model Context Protocol server so AI assistants can drive it. mcp.rs (Rust) detects the Node runtime, syncs the server files, and writes/validates MCP config for Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Codex. The standalone packages/mcp/src/app-db.ts reads the app's SQLite store via the sqlite CLI to expose request history, saved requests, and default headers to the server — redacting sensitive keys on the way out.

tour.title: Build & Runtime Config
tour.description: Two manifests tie the runtime together. package.json defines project metadata, the dev/build scripts, and the React 19 + Tauri 2 dependency tree for the frontend. tauri.conf.json configures the desktop shell — product name, version, build commands, window settings, bundling, and plugins — and is what turns the React app and Rust backend from Steps 2-9 into a single packaged desktop application.

tour.title: Continuous Integration
tour.description: As a capstone, the CI workflow shows how the whole project is verified. On every push to main and pull request it runs a TypeScript typecheck and the JS test suites on Ubuntu, plus Rust cargo tests on macOS — exercising both halves of the codebase you have just toured. This cross-platform matrix reflects that Penguin is a desktop app whose frontend and Rust backend must both pass before release.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions YAML: 'on' declares triggers (push/pull_request), and separate jobs run in parallel across OS runners. Splitting JS and Rust onto Ubuntu and macOS validates the codebase the way it actually ships.
